title: Same task, different style
intro: You ask Claude to add input validation to a signup form. Pick an output style and see how the reply changes.

show.title: Default
show.detail: No style is selected: Claude does the work and explains it in its usual way.

trace.text: Adds validation and describes the changes.

show.title: Concise
show.detail: Claude leads with the result and skips narration about each step.

trace.text: Validation added to the email and password fields. Tests pass.

show.title: Explanatory
show.detail: Claude does the work and adds short insight notes about why the code is built the way it is.

trace.text: Adds validation, then an Insight note on validating on both client and server.

show.title: Learning
show.detail: Claude does part of the work and leaves small pieces marked TODO(human) for you to write.

trace.text: Writes the form wiring and leaves the password rule as TODO(human).

quiz.question: Where can you save your own output style for one project?
quiz.explanation: Custom styles are Markdown files in .claude/output-styles for a project, or ~/.claude/output-styles for all your projects.
